svg.text: THE AUDIT TRAIL (appendix): what a reader must be able to check

text.style: font-family:'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;font-size:10.8px;

svg.text: Coding frame with counts · dated analytic memos · the decision log (which candidate themes were merged, renamed or dropped) ·

text.style: font-family:'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;font-size:10.8px;

svg.text: the theme table with a defining statement and an extract for each · the negative-case note · the reflexive statement

text.style: font-family:'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;font-size:10px;font-weight:400;

svg.text: None of these is required by reflexive TA's logic in the positivist sense; all of them are what makes the account checkable by an examiner.

text.style: font-family:'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;font-size:10.2px;font-weight:400;

svg.text: Themes are not "found in" the data. They are constructed by an analyst whose history and training are part of the instrument.

text.style: font-family:'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;font-size:10.2px;font-weight:400;

svg.text: A theme must be able to be wrong: it should be sayable what evidence would have contradicted it — and that evidence reported if it occurred.

text.style: font-family:'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;font-size:10.5px;font-weight:600;

svg.text: Six phases, one sentence of data, one audit trail — and one negative case that the account keeps.
